# Section 2: Mission

Section 2 contains one standard addressing the institution's mission.

## Standard 2.1 — Institutional Mission [CR] {.core-requirement}

::: {.callout-important}
## Core Requirement
This is a Core Requirement — one of the most fundamental aspects of institutional quality.
:::

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

The institution has a clearly defined and published mission appropriate to higher education that guides its activities.

### Typical Evidence Types

- Current mission statement
- Board minutes showing mission approval/review
- Strategic plan referencing mission
- Catalog and website showing published mission
- Examples of mission-driven decisions

### Suggested Owners

- President's Office
- Strategic Planning Committee
- Institutional Effectiveness Office

### Common Pitfalls / Weak Evidence

- Mission statement not recently reviewed
- Mission not visible on website or in catalog
- Cannot demonstrate how mission guides decisions
- Mission inappropriate for institution type

### Example Practices

- Regular mission review cycle (every 3-5 years)
- Mission prominently displayed on campus and online
- Strategic plan explicitly tied to mission
- Budget requests require mission alignment statement

### Reflective Prompts

- When was our mission last reviewed and by whom?
- Where is our mission published?
- Can we provide examples of decisions guided by our mission?
- Does our mission appropriately reflect who we are and whom we serve?

::: {.callout-note title="NC Considerations"}
North Carolina community colleges operate within the NC Community College System and must align with both local and state missions. Ensure your mission reflects:

- Open-door policy
- Workforce development focus
- Community service emphasis
- Your unique institutional identity
- Your specific service area
:::
